Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

schema.description: A step-up approver's signed statement: for one subject, at one relying party, over one challenge the relying party issued, for one purpose, bound to one value. Issued and proved by the approver's did:key and carried embedded, as an open object, in the document it backs; never sent on its own. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

audience.description: The relying party's DID. MUST equal the document's recipient and the verifier's own DID.

boundTo.description: The opaque value the statement is bound to, compared by equality with the relying party's pending record. For `stepUp`, the approve-request's `boundTo` (a salted DigestMultibase of the operation). For `decision`, the decision's `payloadDigest`. For `enrol`, the enrolment id — an enrollmentId, a claimId, or the terms digest auth/step-up/approver/enroll/0.1 defines.

challenge.description: The relying party's challenge for this ceremony, copied verbatim: the approve-request's challenge for `stepUp`, the decision's `challenge` for `decision`, the enrolment start's challenge for `enrol`.

purpose.description: What the statement attests. `stepUp`: a re-authentication bound to one operation (carried in auth/step-up/approve-response/0.7). `decision`: the factor backing a consent decision (carried in task-consent/decision/0.2 `evidence`). `enrol`: proof of possession of the approver key at enrolment. Signed, so a statement made for one use is refused at another.

subject.description: The one subject DID the approver acts for. MUST equal the subject bound to the relying party's pending record, and MUST differ from the document's issuer.

schema.title: Auth — Step-up Approver Attest — payload
